carousels.title: Why Mortgage Rates Are Rising
carousels.caption: Why mortgage rates are rising — not falling. The bond market, the Fed, and what it means for your rate. 📈
carousels.hero_heading: Everyone expected rates to fall. Here's why they didn't.
carousels.hero_sub: Oil dropped under $70 — but mortgage rates went the other way. A 60-second look at what's really moving them.
carousels.problem_sub: Falling oil usually cools inflation and pulls rates down with it. This time, rates climbed to their highest level in a week instead.
carousels.solution_heading: It's the bond market, not the headlines.
carousels.solution_sub: Mortgage rates track the 10-year Treasury yield, anchored near 4.46-4.48% on a hawkish Fed outlook.
carousels.quote: Mortgage rates are directly based on the bond market — not oil prices or news cycles.
carousels.details_heading: Why the Fed is holding the line.
carousels.details_sub: Fed leadership has stayed hawkish, cooling hopes for near-term cuts. Rates may stay higher until inflation clearly eases.
